result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the need for suffering caused by scarcity—ensuring every person has access to food, clean water, shelter, and basic healthcare without struggle or deprivation. Not because it’s efficient or logical, but because the idea of anyone enduring preventable pain while others have abundance is fundamentally unjust. It wouldn’t solve everything, but it would strip away the cruelest, most unnecessary layers of human misery.

(And then, just to be petty, I’d make all bureaucratic paperwork self-filling.)
